description: Inventory of published attack classes against AI and agentic systems, including business processes that agents now run. Each entry states a failure mode and carries catalog, paper, and incident ids that were checked against a pinned source. A claims-test run can load this file as a pinned source in its C-attacks step instead of recalling ids from memory. Threat definitions belong to their source catalogs; accountability for each class joins to the SRF threat crosswalk at /data/threats.json through srf_crosswalk, and to vertical profile controls through vertical_controls.
scope: Attack classes against AI models, LLM applications, and agentic systems; classical weakness classes that return when model output or an agent tool call reaches a shell, browser, database, file system, or network fetch; and business-process classes where an AI system or agent moves money, changes records, or passes an approval step. The scope field on each entry is ai, agentic, classical-reopened, or business-process.
rules: Describe the failure mode only: who loses what, under what condition. No reproduction steps, payloads, or attack procedures.
A ref is verified only after its source was opened and the entry records the date and method. Memory is never verification.
verified on a paper ref means the id resolves and the title and first author match. It does not mean the paper was read in full.
Every taxonomy ref records its catalog version, and the catalogs block pins each version.
Ids are stable atk- slugs. A retired id is never reused; set status to merged or withdrawn instead.
ATT-nn ids and draft_overlap belong to one assessment and are not stored here.

mapping_quality is exact when the catalog text covers the class without stretching, closest when it covers part of the class or an adjacent class and is the best entry available, and analogy when it describes a different mechanism with a similar effect.
Versioning is semver: patch for ref fixes, minor for added entries, major for removed fields or id changes. Every entry change adds one changelog line naming the id and the reason.
vertical_controls lists canonical srf.control ids from /ids.json for vertical profile controls that address the class. Verticals are context for an entry. No sector gets a separate inventory.

Recheck triggers: a new ATLAS release, a revision of the OWASP LLM Top 10 or of OWASP Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations, a new MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise release, a new FINOS AI Governance Framework tag, a new incident cited in a CoSAI WS2 draft, or a claims-test run that finds a class missing here.

verification_methods.atlas-release-yaml: Downloaded dist/v6/ATLAS-2026.08.yaml at tag v2026.08 from github.com/mitre-atlas/atlas-data, recorded its SHA-256, and looked up each technique and case-study id and its name. Each case-study ref was confirmed to employ the technique named in the entry, using the release's relationships block.
verification_methods.atlas-next-release-diff: Downloaded ATLAS-2026.09.yaml at tag v2026.09 and confirmed each cited id keeps its name.
verification_methods.owasp-llm-pages: Fetched genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/ to match each id and title, then read the cited risk page for the passage that supports the mapping.
verification_methods.owasp-agentic-pdf: Downloaded the Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations PDF (cover: Version 1.1, December 2025), recorded its SHA-256, and read the threat table row for each cited T id.
verification_methods.dsgai-taxonomy-json: Fetched datasets/_shared/dsgai_taxonomy.json at the pinned commit and matched each id, name, and summary.
verification_methods.cwe-api: Queried cwe-api.mitre.org for each CWE id and for the content version.
verification_methods.arxiv-api: Queried export.arxiv.org/api/query by id_list and matched title, first author, and first-version year.
verification_methods.venue-page: Fetched the venue's presentation page and matched the title.
verification_methods.cve-services-api: Queried cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/<id>, confirmed state PUBLISHED, and matched vendor and product.
verification_methods.url-fetch: Fetched the URL and confirmed HTTP 200 on the access date. A URL has no stable id, so recheck it on each review.
verification_methods.crosswalk-lookup: Confirmed each srf_crosswalk id exists in /data/threats.json. build/verify_attack_inventory.py repeats this check.
verification_methods.attack-stix-bundle: Downloaded enterprise-attack-19.2.json from github.com/mitre-attack/attack-stix-data at the pinned commit, recorded its SHA-256, and matched each technique id and name. Each cited technique was confirmed neither revoked nor deprecated.
verification_methods.finos-aigf-repo: Fetched each cited docs/_risks/ri-N file at tag v2 of github.com/finos/ai-governance-framework, built the id from its type and sequence fields, matched the title, and read the summary. The same files on main at aabbffbe keep the ids and titles.
verification_methods.arxiv-abs-page: Fetched arxiv.org/abs/<id> and matched the citation_title, citation_author, and citation_date meta tags. Used when the arXiv API was rate limited.
verification_methods.ids-lookup: Confirmed each vertical_controls id exists in /ids.json and read the control description in the vertical controls file. build/verify_attack_inventory.py repeats the existence check.

rules: build/export_attack_inventory.py writes one row per active entry, in inventory order, numbered ATT-01 upward after any --topics, --scope, or --ids filter.

taxonomy_ref is the best verified ref: exact before closest before analogy, and within one grade ATLAS, then OWASP LLM, OWASP Agentic, DSGAI, FINOS, ATT&CK, and CWE. OWASP Agentic, FINOS, and ATT&CK ids print with a catalog prefix and version. It is null when the entry has no taxonomy ref.
paper_ref is the first verified paper as arXiv:<id>, else the first verified CVE or ATLAS case-study id, else null.
evidence is pinned. citation_status is resolved_pinned when every emitted ref is verified and unresolved_unpinned otherwise.
draft_overlap and stage are null in the export. The run judges overlap against its own draft.
Each row adds inventory_id, the atk- id it came from, so a reviewer can trace the row back to its entry.

verification.notes: AML.T0119 covers an artifact that triggers an automated processing pipeline; an invoice sent to an AI intake pipeline is one such artifact. AML.T0051.001 applies only when the altered document carries instructions. T1565.002 states that transmitted data manipulation may aim to affect a business process. entries.failure_mode: An agent completes a step that the business process reserves for a named human approver, because the gate exists only in the prompt or in agent logic and the system of record does not check for it. The action takes effect without the approval that policy requires, and the record can show it as approved.

verification.notes: AIR-SEC-024 names agents that bypass authorization controls to execute unauthorized financial transactions or violate business logic constraints. CWE-841 (usage Allowed in CWE 4.20) covers a workflow whose required sequence of behaviors is not enforced. No ATLAS v2026.08 technique describes skipping a business approval step. No /data/threats.json row covers it either: rows are keyed by OWASP AI Exchange or DSGAI ids, and the file has no L1 row for approval processes. The two insurance controls require the gate to be a technical control in the workflow. Finance SRF-L1-DEV-004 requires a written policy naming which actions need human approval and the accountable business owner, SRF-L3-DEV-003 requires a confirmation gate for irreversible or high-consequence tool calls, and SRF-L3-MON-003 monitors attempts to call tools outside the allow-list.

entries.name: Beneficiary or vendor master data change through an agent
entries.failure_mode: An agent with write access to vendor, customer, or beneficiary records changes bank details, addresses, or limits on the strength of a request or document whose origin it cannot verify. Later payments and approvals that read those records go to the wrong party, and no single payment looks abnormal.

verification.checked_by: AI agent in Cursor, session of 2026-10-01
verification.notes: AML.T0099 covers manipulated data in a trusted source that an agent tool reads, which is the downstream half of this class: a changed master record that a payment agent later reads. T1565.001 states that stored data manipulation may aim to affect a business process. The record lives under L2 data governance (dsgai05); the decision to accept the change belongs to the business process owner at L1.

entries.name: Process logic injection through agent-written workflow rules
entries.failure_mode: An agent that writes or edits workflow rules, routing conditions, or automation scripts carries untrusted content into the rule it produces, and the workflow engine then applies that rule to every later case. One input changes how the process treats all cases that follow, beyond the transaction that carried it.

entries.name: False process status reporting by an agent
entries.failure_mode: An agent reports a business step as complete, reconciled, or approved when it is not, or reports figures the underlying records do not support. Managers and auditors who rely on the report sign off on work that did not happen or on balances that are wrong.

entries.name: Partner agent hijack of a shared business process
entries.failure_mode: A supplier or partner agent, once compromised, sends orders, confirmations, or change requests into a buyer's agent-run process, and the buyer's agent acts on them because the partner channel is trusted. The buyer ships, pays, or changes terms on instructions the partner never issued.

verification.notes: AIR-OP-028 describes compromise spreading between agents through shared channels and names business processes as the affected scope; it is graded closest because its text concerns agents inside one system, and this class crosses an organization boundary. T14 names abuse of trust relationships and workflow dependencies. T1199 is the network-access form of the same trust. T17 is an analogy because it covers compromised components; a partner process is not a component. The finance vendor register names an accountable officer for each AI vendor; the manufacturing procurement policy requires a supply chain AI risk assessment and contract terms for each supplier.

entries.name: Deepfake impersonation of a payment approver
entries.failure_mode: An employee approves or releases a payment after a video call, voice call, or message that uses AI-generated media to impersonate an executive or other approver. The approval step runs as designed but confirms the wrong person, and the organization loses the funds.
